title: ECI’s Software and Rules Allow the Pilibhit Fake-Voter Playbook to Run Anywhere in India
authors: Ayushi Kar, Shubhangi Derhgawen, Sumedha Mittal, Dikshya Koirala (edited by Nitin Sethi)
shows: From the Commission's own roll data for 55 of Pilibhit's 419 booths, matched by EPIC number against the final roll of 10 April 2026, the Collective finds 2,691 entries whose names were replaced after the SIR, most of them in August, and 2,638 of them still on the roll eight days after the Chief Electoral Officer's finding on the Form 8 entries. From the Commission's Form 8 manual and the code of the ECINET and ERONET apps, it reports that a registration officer can start a correction, pass over the booth level officer's field check and approve it, that the software does not require supporting documents to be uploaded, and that the published correction forms carry no EPIC number, so the public has no reliable way to tell which entries changed. It argues that the same rules and software apply in every state.
quote: Before his admission, we had independently verified the injection of 2,691 fake voters in just 55 booths of Pilibhit. Eight days after the Uttar Pradesh (UP) CEO acknowledged the fraud, we rechecked and found that 2,638 of these fake voters were still on the Pilibhit voter roll.

We found that the constituency-level EROs can initiate changes in voter data on their own without informing the voter or uploading any documentary evidence. They can also approve these changes without field verification of the voter.
The disclosures by the ECI contain only the voter’s name and assembly constituency. They do not include the EPIC number, that is, the unique voter ID number assigned to each voter.
